turns.content: Let n>=3 and m>=n+1. Place m marbles of colours C_1,...,C_n around a circle. A cyclic gap is the distance from one occurrence of C_i to the next occurrence of C_i. What restriction is imposed on these gaps, and how many occurrences of C_i are required?
Call m n-colourful if there is a circular arrangement in which every block of n+1 consecutive marbles contains all n colours. Apply the bound for each colour to obtain a necessary inequality for m.
Is that inequality also sufficient? Construct a circular arrangement whenever it holds and verify that every block of n+1 marbles contains all colours.
Check the construction at the join between its last and first marbles. Why do blocks crossing that join still meet the colour requirement?
Combine the counting bound with the construction to state an exact criterion for a length m to be n-colourful.
Set q=ceil(m/(n+1)). For a fixed integer q, combine its defining inequalities with the criterion just proved to give the interval of lengths m that are not n-colourful.
Keeping the block length n+1, determine exactly which of those integer intervals are nonempty and find their largest possible endpoint.
Conclude that only finitely many positive integers are not n-colourful and give the largest one, explaining why it fails and why every larger integer works.
